name: Andy Burnham
role: Prime Minister & First Lord of the Treasury
bio: Former Mayor of Greater Manchester (2017–2026) and former Cabinet minister. Elected Labour Leader on July 16, 2026, and appointed Prime Minister on July 20, 2026, following Keir Starmer's resignation.
keyStance: Establishing a National Care Service, regional devolution and Northern powerhouse investment, public ownership of water and energy, and reforming long-term pension structures with a 2030 double lock.

name: Louise Haigh
role: First Secretary of State, Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster & Minister for the Cabinet Office
bio: Senior Cabinet minister and de facto deputy to the Prime Minister, overseeing civil service delivery, cross-government missions, and constitutional devolution.
keyStance: Cross-Whitehall delivery, public sector productivity, regional transport integration, and strengthening devolved Combined Authorities.

name: John Healey
role: Chancellor of the Exchequer
bio: Appointed Chancellor of the Exchequer by Andy Burnham in July 2026 to lead HM Treasury and economic strategy, transitioning from his previous role as Defence Secretary.
keyStance: Balancing fiscal credibility with regional capital investment, protecting low-income pensioners from personal allowance tax drag, and funding the National Care Service.

name: Ed Miliband
role: Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs
bio: Former Labour Leader and Energy Secretary promoted to Foreign Secretary in July 2026, spearheading international climate diplomacy and European security cooperation.
keyStance: Global clean energy pacts, deepening European defence and trade partnerships, NATO collective deterrence, and international diplomatic mediation.

name: Shabana Mahmood
role: Home Secretary
bio: Appointed Home Secretary in September 2025 and retained by Andy Burnham in July 2026 to lead policing, border security, counter-terrorism, and immigration enforcement.
keyStance: Expanding the Border Security Command, restoring visible neighbourhood policing, dismantling organized people-smuggling networks, and clearing asylum backlogs.

name: Wes Streeting
role: Secretary of State for Defence
bio: Moved from Health to become Defence Secretary in July 2026, leading the Strategic Defence Review implementation, armed forces modernization, and NATO readiness.
keyStance: Meeting the 2.5% of GDP defence spending trajectory, sovereign UK defence industrial procurement, and unwavering military backing for Ukraine and NATO allies.

name: Yvette Cooper
role: Secretary of State for Health and Social Care
bio: Senior Cabinet stateswoman appointed Health and Social Care Secretary in July 2026 to architect Burnham's flagship National Care Service and cut NHS waiting lists.
keyStance: Integrating adult social care with the NHS via a National Care Service, slashing elective waiting times, and expanding community mental health hubs.

name: Alex Norris
role: Lord Chancellor & Secretary of State for Justice
bio: Promoted to Lord Chancellor and Justice Secretary in July 2026, overseeing the courts service, prison capacity reform, probation, and constitutional law.
keyStance: Clearing Crown Court backlogs, modernizing custodial rehabilitation, strengthening victims' rights, and upholding the rule of law.

name: Lucy Powell
role: Secretary of State for Education
bio: Key Manchester parliamentarian appointed Education Secretary in July 2026, driving early years expansion, SEND reform, and technical skills pathways.
keyStance: Recruiting 6,500 specialist teachers, expanding funded nursery childcare, overhauling SEND provision, and creating technical excellence colleges.

name: Pat McFadden
role: Secretary of State for Work and Pensions
bio: Experienced Cabinet strategist serving as Work and Pensions Secretary, leading labour market activation, Jobcentre reform, and pension security.
keyStance: Reforming Jobcentres into a National Jobs and Careers Service, tackling economic inactivity through health support, and reviewing long-term state pension sustainability.

name: Jonathan Reynolds
role: Secretary of State for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade
bio: Senior Greater Manchester MP heading the expanded super-department combining Business, Trade, Science, Innovation, and Industrial Strategy.
keyStance: Long-term modern industrial strategy, resetting EU veterinary and touring trade friction, backing British steel and AI R&D, and reforming business rates.

name: Angela Rayner
role: Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government
bio: Returned to the Cabinet under Andy Burnham in July 2026 to spearhead council and social housing delivery, planning reform, and regional devolution.
keyStance: Delivering 1.5 million new homes, biggest generation boost to social and council housing, ending Section 21 no-fault evictions, and empowering regional mayors.

name: Miatta Fahnbulleh
role: Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero
bio: Economist and former New Economics Foundation chief executive promoted to Energy Security and Net Zero Secretary in July 2026.
keyStance: Scaling up Great British Energy public investment, nationwide Warm Homes insulation rollout, accelerating grid connections, and clean power by 2030.

name: Heidi Alexander
role: Secretary of State for Transport
bio: Former London Deputy Mayor for Transport serving as Transport Secretary, overseeing Great British Railways and regional bus franchising.
keyStance: Bringing passenger rail operators into public ownership under Great British Railways, empowering councils to franchise local buses, and delivering Northern Powerhouse Rail.

name: Angela Eagle
role: Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
bio: Veteran parliamentarian appointed DEFRA Secretary in July 2026, leading water utility restructuring, flood resilience, and farming support.
keyStance: Enforcing strict statutory penalties on water company sewage discharges, transitioning failing water utilities toward public-benefit models, and backing British food security.

name: Lisa Nandy
role: Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport
bio: Continued as Culture, Media and Sport Secretary under Andy Burnham with an expanded digital inclusion and regional creative economy remit.
keyStance: Independent football governance regulator, regional creative industry investment outside London, protecting public service broadcasting, and grassroots youth facilities.

name: Douglas Alexander
role: Secretary of State for Scotland
bio: Experienced former Cabinet minister serving as Scotland Secretary, coordinating UK government industrial investment and energy transition across Scotland.
keyStance: Headquartering Great British Energy in Aberdeen, strengthening collaborative intergovernmental working with Holyrood, and boosting Scottish clean energy jobs.

name: Stephen Kinnock
role: Secretary of State for Wales
bio: Promoted to Secretary of State for Wales in July 2026, championing Welsh industrial decarbonisation, steel transition support, and Senedd partnership.
keyStance: Securing green steel transition investment at Port Talbot, upgrading Welsh rail connectivity, and working closely with the Welsh Government.

name: Chris Bryant
role: Secretary of State for Northern Ireland
bio: Promoted to Northern Ireland Secretary in July 2026, overseeing Stormont power-sharing stability, Windsor Framework implementation, and reconciliation.
keyStance: Supporting stable devolved government at Stormont, pragmatic SPS veterinary trade facilitation across the Irish Sea, and legacy reconciliation.

name: Emma Reynolds
role: Chief Secretary to the Treasury
bio: Promoted from Economic Secretary to Chief Secretary to the Treasury in July 2026, managing public spending reviews and departmental capital budgets.
keyStance: Multi-year departmental spending settlements, capital investment in regional transport and housing, and value-for-money public procurement.

name: Sir Alan Campbell
role: Lord President of the Council & Leader of the House of Commons
bio: Former Government Chief Whip serving as Leader of the House of Commons, managing the government's legislative timetable and parliamentary standards.
keyStance: Delivering the King's Speech legislative programme, strengthening the Commons Modernisation Committee, and tightening rules on MP outside lobbying.

name: Baroness Smith of Basildon
role: Lord Privy Seal & Leader of the House of Lords
bio: Long-serving Labour peers' leader retained as Leader of the House of Lords in July 2026 to steer constitutional and legislative reform through the upper chamber.
keyStance: Abolishing remaining hereditary peerages, paving the way for an elected Assembly of the Nations and Regions, and scrutinizing statutory instruments.

name: Ellie Reeves KC
role: Attorney General for England and Wales
bio: Barrister and former Labour Party Chair promoted to Attorney General in July 2026, serving as chief legal adviser to the Crown and attending Cabinet.
keyStance: Upholding domestic and international rule of law, strengthening Crown Prosecution Service capacity on violence against women and girls, and prosecuting fraud.

name: Anneliese Midgley
role: Parliamentary Secretary to the Treasury (Government Chief Whip)
bio: Former trade union political director appointed Government Chief Whip in July 2026, overseeing parliamentary management and party cohesion.
keyStance: Maintaining legislative cohesion across the 403-strong Labour parliamentary caucus and connecting backbench constituency priorities with Downing Street.

name: Kirsty McNeill
role: Minister of State for International Development (Attending Cabinet)
bio: Former executive director at Save the Children promoted to attend Cabinet as International Development Minister in July 2026.
keyStance: Rebuilding multilateral humanitarian partnerships, climate adaptation finance for developing nations, and global health security initiatives.

name: Kemi Badenoch
role: Leader of the Opposition & Conservative Leader
bio: Elected Conservative Party leader in November 2024. Reshuffled her Shadow Cabinet in 2026 to sharpen economic, foreign policy, and public service accountability.
keyStance: Roll back state intervention, defend family enterprise and farming inheritance reliefs, dismantle civil service quangos, and enforce strict border caps.

name: Alex Burghart
role: Deputy Leader of the Opposition, Shadow Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster & Shadow Secretary of State for Northern Ireland
bio: Appointed Deputy Leader of the Opposition in 2026 alongside his Cabinet Office and Northern Ireland briefs, leading cross-departmental scrutiny.
keyStance: Scrutinizing Cabinet Office delivery, defending the constitutional integrity of the Union, and opposing Whitehall regulatory expansion.

name: Andrew Griffith
role: Shadow Chancellor of the Exchequer
bio: Former FTSE 100 CFO and City Minister promoted to Shadow Chancellor in Kemi Badenoch's 2026 reshuffle to lead Conservative fiscal and enterprise policy.
keyStance: Slashing business taxes and regulatory red tape, reversing employer National Insurance hikes, defending the pensions triple lock, and curbing state borrowing.

name: Tom Tugendhat
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs
bio: Former Security Minister and Foreign Affairs Committee Chair appointed Shadow Foreign Secretary in 2026, bringing hawkish security and diplomatic expertise.
keyStance: Robust deterrence against Russian, Chinese, and Iranian state threats, strengthening NATO and AUKUS alliances, and resisting EU regulatory alignment.

name: Chris Philp
role: Shadow Home Secretary
bio: Former Policing and Crime Minister serving as Shadow Home Secretary, focusing on border deterrence, immigration caps, and frontline policing.
keyStance: Binding annual parliamentary cap on net migration, third-country offshore asylum deterrence, and expanded stop-and-search powers against knife crime.

name: James Cartlidge
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Defence
bio: Former Defence Procurement Minister leading Conservative scrutiny of military readiness, munitions stockpiles, and defence spending.
keyStance: Legislate 3.0% of GDP defence spending by 2030, ring-fence the Dreadnought nuclear deterrent, and reverse reductions in regular British Army personnel.

name: Damian Hinds
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Health and Social Care
bio: Experienced former Cabinet minister appointed Shadow Health and Social Care Secretary in 2026 to challenge Labour's National Care Service and NHS waiting times.
keyStance: Demanding NHS management productivity reforms over bureaucracy, expanding Pharmacy First, and protecting independent social care providers.

name: Nick Timothy
role: Shadow Lord Chancellor & Shadow Secretary of State for Justice
bio: Former Downing Street Chief of Staff appointed Shadow Justice Secretary in February 2026, leading policy on judicial sovereignty and sentencing.
keyStance: Reasserting parliamentary supremacy over foreign courts, ending early prison release schemes, and enforcing mandatory custodial sentences for prolific offenders.

name: Laura Trott
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Education
bio: Former Chief Secretary to the Treasury spearheading Conservative policy on school standards, free schools, and repealing VAT on independent education.
keyStance: Defending academic standards and multi-academy trusts, repealing the 20% VAT on independent school fees, and expanding high-skill degree apprenticeships.

name: Helen Whately
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Work and Pensions
bio: Former Social Care and Treasury Minister serving as Shadow Work and Pensions Secretary, leading Conservative plans to cut the welfare bill and protect pensioners.
keyStance: Tightening sickness and disability benefit eligibility to curb economic inactivity, restoring Universal Winter Fuel Payments, and maintaining the pensions triple lock.

name: Claire Coutinho
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade
bio: Appointed to the expanded Shadow Business, Innovation, Science and Trade brief in 2026 (with Julia Lopez covering during maternity leave).
keyStance: Repealing burdensome employment regulations, cutting industrial energy costs, championing UK tech and AI innovation, and pursuing bilateral free trade deals.

name: Katie Lam
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government
bio: Rising 2024 intake MP promoted to Shadow Housing and Communities Secretary in 2026, defending green belt protections and gentle urban densification.
keyStance: Protecting rural green belt land from top-down Whitehall housing targets, prioritizing brownfield urban regeneration, and cutting stamp duty for first-time buyers.

name: Andrew Bowie
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero
bio: Former Nuclear and Networks Minister promoted to Shadow Energy Secretary in 2026, championing North Sea oil and gas and nuclear baseload power.
keyStance: Backing annual North Sea oil and gas licensing, accelerating Small Modular Reactors (SMRs), and opposing punitive Net Zero levies on households.

name: Richard Holden
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Transport
bio: Former Roads Minister and Party Chairman appointed Shadow Transport Secretary in 2026, campaigning for motorists and against rail nationalisation.
keyStance: Backing motorists against punitive road pricing and 20mph blanket zones, ring-fencing pothole repair funds, and defending private open-access rail competition.

name: Victoria Atkins
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
bio: Rural Lincolnshire MP and former Cabinet minister leading the Conservative defence of British farmers and rural communities.
keyStance: Reversing the family farm inheritance tax changes in full, protecting prime agricultural land from solar sprawl, and Increasing the UK farming budget.

name: Rebecca Paul
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport
bio: Promoted to the Shadow Cabinet in 2026 to lead on media freedom, heritage protection, BBC licence fee scrutiny, and grassroots sport.
keyStance: Defending free speech and press freedom, scrutinizing BBC impartiality, opposing ideological rewrites of British heritage, and backing grassroots sport.

name: Harriet Cross
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Scotland
bio: North East Scotland MP promoted to Shadow Scotland Secretary in 2026, championing the Union, North Sea energy jobs, and rural Scottish enterprise.
keyStance: Defending Scotland's place in the UK, reversing the Energy Profits Levy windfall tax to save Aberdeen energy jobs, and opposing SNP tax divergence.

name: Mims Davies
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Wales
bio: Serving as Shadow Secretary of State for Wales, holding both the UK and Welsh Labour governments to account on NHS waiting lists and transport.
keyStance: Scrapping default 20mph speed limits in Wales, auditing Welsh NHS performance, and protecting Welsh upland livestock farmers.

name: Richard Fuller
role: Shadow Chief Secretary to the Treasury
bio: Former Economic Secretary to the Treasury serving as Shadow Chief Secretary, leading line-by-line scrutiny of public expenditure and civil service headcount.
keyStance: Returning civil service headcount to pre-pandemic levels, halting wasteful public sector consultancy spend, and enforcing strict fiscal rules.

name: Joy Morrissey
role: Shadow Minister for Women and Equalities
bio: Promoted to the Shadow Cabinet in 2026 as Shadow Minister for Women and Equalities, campaigning to protect biological sex definitions in law.
keyStance: Clarifying the Equality Act to protect single-sex spaces and women's sports based on biological sex, and removing ideological DEI quotas from public bodies.

name: Kevin Hollinrake
role: Conservative Party Chairman (Attending Shadow Cabinet)
bio: Former Post Office and Small Business Minister appointed Conservative Party Chairman to rebuild local associations and campaign infrastructure.
keyStance: Rebuilding Conservative grassroots campaigning, championing high street entrepreneurs, and holding Labour councils to account on council tax hikes.

name: Neil O'Brien
role: Shadow Minister for Policy Renewal (Attending Shadow Cabinet)
bio: Policy thinker and former Levelling Up Minister appointed by Kemi Badenoch to coordinate long-term Conservative policy renewal across all commissions.
keyStance: Data-driven critique of migration fiscal impacts, wiring pro-growth planning and energy reforms, and developing the next Conservative manifesto.

name: Jesse Norman
role: Shadow Leader of the House of Commons
bio: Former Treasury and Transport Minister serving as Shadow Leader of the House of Commons, defending parliamentary scrutiny against executive overreach.
keyStance: Ensuring full parliamentary debate on primary legislation, defending backbench rights, and opposing constitutional gerrymandering.

name: Lord True
role: Shadow Leader of the House of Lords
bio: Experienced constitutional peer leading the Conservative benches in the House of Lords.
keyStance: Defending the revising role of the House of Lords, scrutinizing government bills line by line, and opposing partisan constitutional upheaval.

name: Dame Rebecca Harris
role: Opposition Chief Whip
bio: Experienced former Government whip serving as Opposition Chief Whip, managing Conservative parliamentary operations in the House of Commons.
keyStance: Coordinating effective parliamentary opposition votes, disciplined scrutiny in Bill committees, and unified frontbench messaging.

name: Nigel Farage
role: Party Leader & MP
bio: Leader of Reform UK and MP for Clacton, who unveiled the party's first official 'Shadow Cabinet' team in February 2026 to signal readiness for government.
keyStance: Freeze non-essential immigration, leave the ECHR, raise personal income tax allowance to £20,000, scrap Net Zero subsidies, and introduce private-public healthcare competition.

name: Richard Tice
role: Deputy Leader & Shadow Secretary of State for Business, Trade and Energy
bio: Deputy Leader appointed to the Business, Trade and Energy brief in February 2026, leading deregulation and industrial economic policy.
keyStance: Cut corporation tax to 15%, lift employer National Insurance thresholds, fast-track North Sea gas and UK shale extraction, and scrap all green levies.

name: Robert Jenrick
role: Shadow Chancellor of the Exchequer
bio: Former Conservative leadership contender and immigration minister who defected to Reform UK, appointed Shadow Chancellor by Nigel Farage in February 2026.
keyStance: Aggressive government spending restraint, abolition of family farm and business inheritance tax, reversing employer National Insurance rises, and lowering fuel duties.

name: Zia Yusuf
role: Shadow Home Secretary
bio: Tech entrepreneur and Reform UK policy lead appointed Shadow Home Secretary in February 2026 to lead border enforcement and immigration policy.
keyStance: Immediate offshore processing and returns for illegal arrivals, leaving the ECHR and Refugee Convention, mass deportations of foreign offenders, and strict work visa quotas.

name: Suella Braverman
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Education, Skills and Equalities
bio: Former Home Secretary and Attorney General who defected to Reform UK, appointed to lead education, skills, and institutional reform in Farage's frontbench team.
keyStance: Repealing the Equality Act, scrapping DEI civil service mandates, shifting 50% of school leavers into technical trades, and protecting freedom of speech.

name: Lee Anderson
role: Chief Whip & Working Class Champion
bio: Former coal miner and deputy party chairman serving as Parliamentary Chief Whip, spearheading working-class voter mobilization and party discipline.
keyStance: Zero tolerance on illegal channel crossings, defunding migrant hotel contracts, tough criminal sentencing, and protecting red-wall industrial jobs.

name: Danny Kruger
role: Head of Preparation for Government & Policy
bio: Leading conservative intellectual and author who joined Reform UK's parliamentary apparatus to head preparations for executive government and legislative drafting.
keyStance: Systemic civil service restructuring, restoring parliamentary sovereignty, institutional reform of regulatory bodies, and local community revitalization.

name: Rupert Lowe
role: Spokesperson for Business, Agriculture & Deregulation
bio: Businessman and former football club chairman campaigning against Whitehall red tape and the regulatory burden on British farming and fishing.
keyStance: Cutting Whitehall administrative staffing by 50%, full protection for agricultural inheritance reliefs, and restoring British coastal fishing rights.

name: Sir Ed Davey
role: Party Leader & MP
bio: Former Energy Secretary who led the Liberal Democrats to a historic 72 MPs in 2024, focusing on health, social care, carer support, and public service renewal.
keyStance: Universal access to GP appointments within 7 days, £5bn free personal adult social care package, ban water executive bonuses, and establish a long-term pathway back to the EU Single Market.

name: Daisy Cooper
role: Deputy Leader & Treasury Spokesperson
bio: Deputy Leader and Treasury Spokesperson, leading the Lib Dem economic scrutiny on fair taxation, cost-of-living support, and public service reinvestment.
keyStance: Fair taxes on bank and tech super-profits, unfreezing income tax thresholds when fiscal space allows, and targeted relief for high street small businesses.

name: Helen Morgan
role: Spokesperson for Health and Social Care
bio: Chartered accountant and by-election victor leading parliamentary campaigns against rural ambulance wait times, hospital corridor care, and dental deserts.
keyStance: Dedicated emergency funding for ambulance response times, guaranteed NHS dental appointments, mental health parity, and free personal social care.

name: Calum Miller
role: Spokesperson for Foreign Affairs
bio: Former senior civil servant with deep international diplomacy and foreign policy background, leading scrutiny of international treaties and European relations.
keyStance: Rebuilding UK-EU institutional partnerships and a bespoke Customs Union, steadfast support for Ukraine, upholding international law, and restoring the 0.7% aid target.

name: Lisa Smart
role: Spokesperson for Home Affairs
bio: Former charity chief executive and local council leader serving as Liberal Democrat Home Affairs Spokesperson.
keyStance: Restoring visible community policing, establishing safe and legal asylum routes alongside rapid fair case processing, and tackling rural and retail crime.

name: James MacCleary
role: Spokesperson for Defence
bio: Experienced local leader elected in 2024 leading defence procurement scrutiny, European defence cooperation, and Armed Forces personnel welfare.
keyStance: Reach 2.5%+ of GDP defence spending responsibly, strengthen the European NATO pillar, reverse troop cuts, and upgrade service family housing.

name: Jess Brown-Fuller
role: Spokesperson for Justice
bio: Chichester MP serving as Liberal Democrat Justice Spokesperson, campaigning to fix the courts backlog and rehabilitate offenders.
keyStance: Clearing the Crown Court backlog, restoring legal aid access, tackling violence against women and girls, and improving prison rehabilitation.

name: Munira Wilson
role: Spokesperson for Education, Children and Families
bio: Leading national voice on education and child welfare, championing free school meals, SEND reform, and youth mental health support in all schools.
keyStance: Extend free school meals to all children in poverty, fund a qualified mental health professional in every school, and urgently overhaul SEND funding.

name: Steve Darling
role: Spokesperson for Work and Pensions
bio: Former Torbay Council Leader and registered blind MP championing disability rights, carers' allowances, and pensioner security.
keyStance: Overhauling the Carer's Allowance cliff-edge, protecting disability welfare support from arbitrary cuts, and defending the state pension triple lock.

name: Sarah Olney
role: Spokesperson for Business and Trade
bio: Chartered accountant leading scrutiny on industrial policy, EU trade barriers, and high street business rates reform.
keyStance: Replace business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, negotiate an EU veterinary and youth mobility agreement, and support SME exporters.

name: Gideon Amos
role: Spokesperson for Housing, Communities and Local Government
bio: Chartered town planner and former head of the Town and Country Planning Association serving as Housing and Communities Spokesperson.
keyStance: Building 150,000 social rent homes a year, community-led infrastructure-first planning, abolishing residential leaseholds, and fair council funding.

name: Pippa Heylings
role: Spokesperson for Energy Security and Net Zero
bio: International environmental and climate change negotiator leading the Lib Dem transition roadmap to clean renewable power.
keyStance: Accelerate community renewable energy, emergency 10-year home insulation programme, upgrade grid capacity, and achieve 90% renewable electricity by 2030.

name: Olly Glover
role: Spokesperson for Transport
bio: Former railway operations and transport professional serving as Liberal Democrat Transport Spokesperson.
keyStance: Freezing rail fares, expanding rural bus services, accelerating EV charging network rollout, and investing in commuter rail electrification.

name: Tim Farron
role: Spokesperson for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
bio: Former party leader and veteran rural champion leading the national campaign against raw sewage dumping and in defence of family farms.
keyStance: Replace Ofwat with a tough Clean Water Authority, transform water firms into public benefit companies, and add £1bn a year to the UK farming budget.

name: Max Wilkinson
role: Spokesperson for Culture, Media and Sport
bio: Former journalist and local councillor leading Liberal Democrat policy on broadcasting, grassroots sport, and creative industries.
keyStance: Protecting free-to-air sporting crown jewels, supporting independent local journalism, and securing reciprocated visa-free touring for UK musicians in Europe.

name: Wendy Chamberlain
role: Chief Whip & Spokesperson for Scotland
bio: Former police officer and long-serving parliamentary leader managing party discipline, employment rights scrutiny, and Scottish affairs.
keyStance: Strict parliamentary standards, electoral reform via proportional representation, flexible working rights, and stronger cooperative Scottish devolution.

name: Zack Polanski
role: Party Leader
bio: Elected Leader of the Green Party of England and Wales in September 2025, succeeding Carla Denyer & Adrian Ramsay. Prominent London Assembly Member and national campaigner for wealth redistribution, electoral reform, and climate justice.
keyStance: Universal Basic Income trials, immediate proportional representation for Westminster, an annual 2% wealth tax on fortunes over £10m, and an immediate statutory halt to all new fossil fuel extraction.

name: Carla Denyer
role: Parliamentary Leader & Spokesperson for Energy, Health & Foreign Affairs
bio: Renewable energy engineer elected MP for Bristol Central in 2024. Following her co-leadership (2021–2025), she leads the 4-member Green parliamentary group in the House of Commons, focusing on public healthcare and progressive taxation.
keyStance: Annual 1% to 2% wealth tax on assets over £10m, statutory municipal rent controls, reversal of NHS privatisation, and scrapping Trident.

name: Adrian Ramsay
role: Parliamentary Spokesperson for Environment, Rural Affairs & Utilities & MP
bio: Environmental strategist elected MP for rural Waveney Valley in 2024 (former co-leader 2021–2025), leading Green parliamentary work on rural infrastructure, agricultural transition, and river health.
keyStance: Protect British biodiversity, bring water monopolies and National Grid into public ownership, halt new oil and gas, and restore rural bus networks.

name: Ellie Chowns
role: Parliamentary Spokesperson for Economy, Welfare, Food & Agriculture & MP
bio: Former MEP and international development specialist elected MP for North Herefordshire in 2024, leading Green scrutiny on trade agreements, agricultural subsidies, and rural river health.
keyStance: Transform agricultural subsidies to reward regenerative farming, enforce strict phosphate limits on industrial poultry units, and progressive ecological tax reform.

name: Siân Berry
role: Parliamentary Spokesperson for Transport, Housing & Democracy & MP
bio: Former London Assembly Member and veteran green campaigner elected MP for Brighton Pavilion in 2024, succeeding Caroline Lucas.
keyStance: Universal rent controls, massive council house construction, public ownership of buses and railways, and votes for 16-year-olds with proportional representation.

name: Mothin Ali
role: Deputy Leader (Communities & Urban Regeneration)
bio: Elected Green Party Deputy Leader in August 2025; community gardener and Leeds councillor campaigning on urban poverty, youth services, and community empowerment.
keyStance: Community wealth building, radical investment in disadvantaged inner-city areas, and vocal anti-austerity campaigning.

name: Rachel Millward
role: Deputy Leader (Local Government & Climate Action)
bio: Elected Green Party Deputy Leader in August 2025; leader of the Alliance for Wealden Council and climate organizer promoting grassroots municipal transition.
keyStance: Decentralised municipal solar and insulation, rural public transport restoration, and empowering local councils with statutory green planning powers.

name: John Swinney
role: Party Leader & First Minister of Scotland
bio: First Minister of Scotland and veteran statesman leading the Scottish Government with focus on child poverty reduction and public services.
keyStance: Scottish self-determination, scrap the two-child benefit cap across the UK, remove Trident nuclear weapons from Scotland, rejoin EU.

name: Stephen Flynn
role: Westminster Parliamentary Group Leader & MP
bio: Leading SNP parliamentarian driving parliamentary scrutiny of energy transition, Scottish budget consequentials, and cost of living.
keyStance: Just transition for North Sea energy workers without cliff-edges, demand full devolution of employment and migration powers.

name: Pete Wishart
role: Deputy Westminster Leader & Spokesperson for Home Affairs and Constitutional Relations
bio: Longest-serving Scottish National Party MP, acting as Deputy Westminster Leader and leading scrutiny on migration, home affairs, and constitutional reform.
keyStance: Tailored Scottish Rural Visa pilot, devolution of immigration powers to Holyrood, and replacing the House of Lords.

name: Kirsty Blackman
role: Westminster Chief Whip & Spokesperson for Work, Pensions & Economy
bio: Experienced Westminster frontbencher holding the UK government to account on welfare reform, pensions indexation, and fiscal policy.
keyStance: Defend the pensions triple lock, repeal punitive universal credit sanctions, and protect disability welfare entitlements from cuts.

name: Dave Doogan
role: Westminster Spokesperson for Defence, Energy Security & Net Zero
bio: Prominent defence and energy spokesperson championing Scottish renewable and North Sea industrial capacity alongside armed forces welfare.
keyStance: Fair grid transmission charges for Scottish renewable generators, protecting North Sea transition jobs, and opposing nuclear weapons based on the Clyde.

name: Brendan O'Hara
role: Westminster Spokesperson for Foreign Affairs, Justice & Culture
bio: Senior SNP foreign affairs spokesperson advocating for international humanitarian law, European re-entry, and creative industries.
keyStance: Immediate return to the European Union and Erasmus+, upholding international law and human rights, and protecting Scottish food and drink exporters.

name: Rhun ap Iorwerth
role: Party Leader & Member of the Senedd
bio: Former BBC journalist and Plaid Cymru leader, uniting the party around fair funding formulas, Welsh NHS renewal, and independence.
keyStance: Replace Barnett formula with needs-based funding (+£1.2bn/yr), reclaim £4bn HS2 rail consequentials, devolve Crown Estate to Wales.

name: Liz Saville Roberts
role: Westminster Group Leader & Spokesperson for Justice, Home Affairs & Defence
bio: Privy Councillor and Westminster leader campaigning for judicial devolution and equal constitutional status for Wales.
keyStance: Devolution of policing and criminal justice to Wales, renewable energy wealth retention for Welsh communities, and constitutional fairness.

name: Ben Lake
role: Westminster Spokesperson for Treasury, Foreign Affairs, Energy & Transport
bio: Respected parliamentary orator and committee member leading Plaid Cymru's financial, energy, and transport policy in Westminster.
keyStance: Fair agricultural funding guaranteed post-Brexit, targeted energy bill support for off-gas grid rural households, and reforming UK fiscal rules.

name: Ann Davies
role: Westminster Spokesperson for Environment, Food, Farming & Work and Pensions
bio: Farmer and local government leader elected MP for Caerfyrddin in 2024, championing family farming communities and Welsh agricultural produce.
keyStance: Protecting family farm inheritance reliefs, imposing strict origin labelling on supermarket meat and dairy, and securing clean river standards.

name: Llinos Medi
role: Westminster Spokesperson for Health, Social Care, Housing, Education & Communities
bio: Former Council Leader elected MP for Ynys Môn in 2024, focusing on rural health inequalities, community regeneration, and youth retention in Welsh heartlands.
keyStance: Targeted funding to recruit rural NHS specialists, community housing trusts for local families, and expanding Welsh language educational provision.

name: Movement Council Executive
role: National Convenor & Constitutional Lead
bio: Civic assembly representing traditionalist British restoration, civil liberties, and free-market constitutionalism.
keyStance: Abolish Net Zero statutes, repeal legislation eroding free speech, constitutional referendums, national industrial revival.

name: Civic Campaign Spokesperson
role: Director of Policy & Enterprise
bio: Independent-minded enterprise advocate campaigning across civic forums for constitutional reform, British sovereign fishing, and deregulation.
keyStance: Radical Whitehall downsizing, dismantling regulatory quangos, repealing onerous Net Zero mandates, and defending family businesses.
